record.original_question: For the hard-core lattice gas on general graphs, what happens at non-small fugacity w: when does one have uniqueness versus nonuniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures as a function of w, what are the large-w Gibbs measures, and are the phase transitions first-order or second-order?

evidence.quote: Finally, one may ask: What happens when the fugacity w is not small? In particular, one would like to understand the uniqueness or nonuniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure as a function of w, the nature of the large-w Gibbs measures, and whether the phase transition(s) is/are first-order or second-order.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a (locally finite, infinite) graph. The hard-core lattice gas on $G$ at activity (fugacity) $w>0$ is the family of probability measures on $\{0,1\}^V$ (where $\sigma_v=1$ means site $v$ is occupied) defined by the formal Gibbs specification: for any finite $\Lambda\subset V$ and any admissible boundary configuration $\eta\in\{0,1\}^{V\setminus\Lambda}$ (i.e., $\eta_u\eta_v=0$ for every edge $\{u,v\}\subset V\setminus\Lambda$), the conditional distribution of $\sigma_\Lambda$ given $\eta$ is
$$\mu_\Lambda^\eta(\sigma_\Lambda)\;=\;\frac{1}{Z_\Lambda^\eta}\,w^{\sum_{v\in\Lambda}\sigma_v}\,\mathbf{1}\!\left[\sigma\text{ is an independent set, i.e. }\sigma_u\sigma_v=0\text{ for every edge }\{u,v\}\right],$$
with $\sigma_v=\eta_v$ for $v\notin\Lambda$. An infinite-volume Gibbs measure at activity $w$ is a probability measure on $\{0,1\}^V$ whose conditional distributions on every finite $\Lambda$ agree (almost surely) with $\mu_\Lambda^{\,\cdot}$.

For a general infinite graph $G$, address the following questions about the phase structure as a function of $w$ in the (possibly large) non-perturbative regime:

(a) Characterize the set $\mathcal{W}_!(G)\subset(0,\infty)$ of activities for which there is a unique infinite-volume Gibbs measure, and the complementary set of activities for which there are multiple Gibbs measures. In particular, determine the structure of the phase-coexistence region for large $w$.

(b) Describe the extremal large-$w$ Gibbs measures: are they supported on (or close to) maximum-density independent sets, and how are they classified in terms of the combinatorial/geometric structure of $G$ (e.g., maximum independent sets, "ground-state" configurations)?

(c) Determine the order of the phase transition(s): at each transition value of $w$, decide whether the transition is first-order (discontinuity in the density $\langle\sigma_v\rangle$ as a function of $w$) or second-order (continuous density with non-smooth higher behavior).

Provide answers in the generality of arbitrary (or suitable broad classes of) infinite graphs $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The large-fugacity phase structure of the hard-core lattice gas is well understood only for specific lattices (e.g., bipartite cases via reflection positivity on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the triangular lattice, regular trees) and remains open in general. Even on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, rigorous results for large $w$ rely on Dobrushin/Pirogov–Sinai-type arguments showing coexistence of two periodic phases, but uniqueness/non-uniqueness throughout intermediate activities and the precise order of transitions on general graphs are not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Phase transition in the hard-core model on Z^2
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous proof of phase coexistence at large activity on the square lattice using Pirogov-Sinai theory; nature of transition not fully characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Large-w phase structure understood only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Hard-core model on general graphs - survey
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses uniqueness thresholds for hard-core Gibbs measures on graphs and trees; many questions about large fugacity behavior remain open on general graphs.
status_evidence.claim: General-graph large-fugacity behavior is an open research direction.
